sections.atGlance: Good when a name is spoken too quickly to type. Open the form, note, or booking screen first.
sections.quickSay: Hold the phone or paper where they can see it. Let them spell, then repeat the letters or show what you typed.
sections.breakdown: Bạn có thể asks can you; đánh vần tên means spell the name; cho tôi được không makes it a polite request.

concreteTravelerValueImproved: turns a title-only spelling page into a real form, pickup, and contact-name clarification moment without dropping repair cards

before.title: Bạn có thể kiểm tra camera an ninh được không?
before.englishTitle: Can you check the security camera?
before.summary: Can you check the security camera?

after.title: Bạn có thể kiểm tra camera an ninh được không?
after.englishTitle: Can you check the security camera?
after.summary: For asking staff to review camera footage after a lost item, wrong bag, room issue, or pickup confusion.

sections.atGlance: Use this at a desk with the time, place, and item visible. The more exact the moment, the easier the ask.
sections.quickSay: Show the receipt, room number, ride screen, or photo first. Then ask for the camera check in one calm sentence.
sections.breakdown: Bạn có thể asks can you; kiểm tra means check; camera an ninh means security camera; được không softens the request.

concreteTravelerValueImproved: replaces generic help copy and bad source glosses with a specific lost-item/security-desk request

before.title: Tôi có thể trả lại nó được không?
before.summary: Can I return it?

after.title: Tôi có thể trả lại nó được không?
after.summary: For asking about a return while the item, receipt, size tag, or payment record is still easy to show.

sections.atGlance: Best before leaving the shop or as soon as you notice the problem. Keep the item visible.
sections.quickSay: Show the item and receipt first. The question gives the seller a clear yes/no before you explain why.
sections.breakdown: Tôi có thể asks can I; trả lại means return or give back; nó means it; được không softens the question.

concreteTravelerValueImproved: grounds the return page in a receipt/item counter moment while preserving exchange and price follow-ups

before.title: Lối ra ở đâu?
before.summary: Where is the exit?

after.title: Lối ra ở đâu?
after.summary: For finding the exit from a market, museum, station, temple, mall, or attraction when signs are not obvious.

sections.atGlance: Ask near a doorway, corridor, ticket area, or crowd flow. Watch for the first gesture after the answer.
sections.quickSay: Keep it short and look where they point. If there are several exits, show the street, pickup point, or map next.
sections.breakdown: Lối ra means exit; ở đâu asks where.

concreteTravelerValueImproved: turns an exit title into a concrete multi-door attraction/station navigation page while keeping sightseeing cards

before.title: Bạn có thể viết thời gian được không?
before.summary: Can you write the time?

after.title: Bạn có thể viết thời gian được không?
after.summary: For getting a pickup time, booking time, closing time, or appointment time written clearly.

sections.atGlance: Use it when a spoken time is too fast, noisy, or easy to mishear.
sections.quickSay: Show the booking, ticket, or notes app. Let them write the time before you ask about where to go.
sections.breakdown: Bạn có thể asks can you; viết thời gian means write the time; được không softens the request.

concreteTravelerValueImproved: fixes a bad price gloss and makes the page about exact written timing rather than generic misunderstanding

before.title: Đây có phải là con số đúng không?
before.summary: Is this the right number?

after.title: Đây có phải là con số đúng không?
after.summary: For confirming a price, phone number, room number, platform, address number, or ticket number before acting.

sections.atGlance: Good when you already have a number on screen or paper and need a quick check.
sections.quickSay: Point to the number you mean. Pause for yes, no, or a correction before paying, calling, boarding, or signing.
sections.breakdown: Đây có phải asks is this; là con số means the number; đúng không asks correct?

concreteTravelerValueImproved: makes number confirmation concrete across travel contexts and fixes the source breakdown start

before.title: Tôi có thể dùng tương ớt được không?
before.summary: Can I have chili sauce?

after.title: Tôi có thể dùng tương ớt được không?
after.summary: For asking for chili sauce at a table, stall, or counter without turning it into a long condiment request.

sections.atGlance: Best when the food is already in front of you or the sauce tray is nearby.
sections.quickSay: Point to the dish or sauce area first. The phrase can mean asking to use or get the chili sauce.
sections.breakdown: Tôi có thể asks can I; dùng tương ớt means use chili sauce; được không softens the request.

concreteTravelerValueImproved: keeps the ready audio while clarifying the have/use nuance and making the table request specific

before.englishTitle: Can I order this without meat?

after.title: Tôi có thể gọi món này mà không có thịt được không?
after.englishTitle: Can I order this without meat?
after.summary: For asking whether a dish can be made without meat before staff starts preparing it.

sections.atGlance: Use it while pointing at the menu item or dish photo. The request needs the exact dish in view.
sections.quickSay: Ask before ordering, then wait for yes, no, or a suggested alternative. Do not bury the meat request inside extra details.
sections.breakdown: Tôi có thể asks can I; gọi món này means order this dish; không có thịt means without meat; được không softens the question.

before.title: Bạn có bia không?
before.summary: Do you have beer?

after.title: Bạn có bia không?
after.summary: For checking whether beer is available at a cafe, food stall, beach bar, or casual restaurant.

sections.atGlance: Best before you settle into ordering drinks. The answer may be a brand, bottle, can, draft, or simple no.
sections.quickSay: Ask once, then point to the drink menu if there is one. Let the staff offer the closest option.
sections.breakdown: Bạn có asks do you have; bia means beer; không turns it into a yes/no question.

concreteTravelerValueImproved: turns a bare drink title into a realistic local drink availability check while preserving drink and checkout cards

before.title: Vui lòng kiểm tra tương tác thuốc
before.summary: Please check for drug interactions

after.title: Vui lòng kiểm tra tương tác thuốc
after.summary: For asking a pharmacist or clinic staff to check whether a new medicine is safe with what you already take.

sections.atGlance: Show the medicine name, package, prescription, or translated note first. This is a safety check, not a casual symptom question.
sections.quickSay: Keep every medicine visible on the counter. Let staff compare names and doses before you add more detail.
sections.breakdown: Vui lòng means please; kiểm tra means check; tương tác thuốc means drug interactions.

concreteTravelerValueImproved: raises a health page from generic symptom scaffolding to a medication-safety counter request with correct source glosses

before.title: Tôi có thể in cái này ở đâu?
before.summary: Where can I print this?

after.title: Tôi có thể in cái này ở đâu?
after.summary: For finding a place to print a document, ticket, visa copy, boarding pass, label, or form.

sections.atGlance: Show the file or screenshot before asking. The goal is directions to a printer, not a long explanation.
sections.quickSay: Lead with the question, then show whether it is on your phone, email, USB drive, or paper.
sections.breakdown: Tôi có thể asks can I; in cái này means print this; ở đâu asks where.

concreteTravelerValueImproved: reframes printing around actual document/travel-paper logistics instead of generic shop-counter language

before.title: Bạn có thể gói nó cẩn thận được không?
before.summary: Can you wrap it carefully?

after.title: Bạn có thể gói nó cẩn thận được không?
after.summary: For asking a seller to wrap a fragile souvenir, gift, bottle, ceramic piece, or small purchase with care.

sections.atGlance: Best while the item is still on the counter and before it goes into the bag.
sections.quickSay: Point to the item and gesture gently if needed. The phrase asks for careful wrapping, not a gift-wrap service.
sections.breakdown: Bạn có thể asks can you; gói nó means wrap it; cẩn thận means carefully; được không softens the request.

concreteTravelerValueImproved: turns wrapping into a fragile-purchase counter moment and fixes bad wrap/carefully source glosses

after.title: Phòng thử đồ ở đâu?

sections.breakdown: Phòng thử đồ means fitting room; ở đâu asks where.

concreteTravelerValueImproved: turns a bare fitting-room question into a clothing-shop moment while preserving shopping follow-up cards

sections.atGlance: Use it at the curb before the ride starts, especially with luggage, a child, or a slow step into traffic.
sections.quickSay: Say it before moving toward the door or seat. Keep the ride screen or destination visible if the driver is checking.
sections.breakdown: Vui lòng means please; đợi tôi means wait for me; lên xe means get in or onto the vehicle.

before.title: Cái này có đậu phộng không?
before.summary: Does this have peanuts?

after.title: Cái này có đậu phộng không?
after.summary: For checking a dish, sauce, topping, or dessert for peanuts before you eat or order.

sections.atGlance: Point to the exact dish or sauce. This question needs the item in view.
sections.quickSay: Ask before eating, then wait for a clear yes, no, or safer recommendation.
sections.breakdown: Cái này means this item; có asks has; đậu phộng means peanuts; không turns it into a yes/no question.

concreteTravelerValueImproved: makes the peanut page a concrete food-safety check while preserving allergy and ingredient cards

before.englishTitle: Can you make it without this ingredient?
before.summary: Can you make it without this ingredient?

after.title: Bạn có thể làm món này không có nguyên liệu này được không?
after.englishTitle: Can you make it without this ingredient?
after.summary: For asking staff to leave out the specific ingredient you are pointing at before they make the dish.

sections.atGlance: Point to the ingredient, menu line, or photo first. The kitchen needs the exact thing to leave out.
sections.quickSay: Ask before ordering and wait for yes, no, or a safer dish. Keep the request short.
sections.breakdown: Bạn có thể asks can you; làm món này means make this dish; không có nguyên liệu này means without this ingredient; được không softens the request.

after.englishTitle: Can you help me contact the embassy?
after.summary: For asking a hotel desk, clinic, police counter, or trusted helper to help contact your embassy.

sections.atGlance: Use it when the next step needs an official contact, not just a local suggestion.

sections.breakdown: Bạn có thể asks can you; giúp tôi means help me; liên hệ với đại sứ quán means contact the embassy; được không softens the request.

after.title: Tôi có thể trả phòng sau được không?

sections.atGlance: Ask while the booking, room number, or key card is visible.
sections.quickSay: Keep it short. The answer may depend on housekeeping, occupancy, or an extra fee.
sections.breakdown: Tôi có thể asks can I; trả phòng means check out; sau means later; được không softens the question.

after.title: Tôi có đi xuống tầng dưới không?
after.summary: For checking whether the route, platform, counter, restroom, or exit is one level below you.

sections.atGlance: Ask while pointing at the stairs, escalator, sign, map, or floor number.

sections.breakdown: Tôi có asks do I; đi xuống means go down; tầng dưới means downstairs or lower floor; không makes it a question.

sections.breakdown: Hãy is a direct please-do opener; gọi means call; cảnh sát means police.

sections.breakdown: Đã có means there has been; một tai nạn means an accident.

before.title: Tôi có cần điền vào mẫu đơn này không?
before.englishTitle: Do I need to fill out this form?
before.summary: Do I need to fill out this form?

after.title: Tôi có cần điền vào mẫu đơn này không?
after.englishTitle: Do I need to fill out this form?
after.summary: For checking whether an arrival, customs, baggage, hotel, or transport form actually needs to be filled before you move on.

sections.atGlance: Hold up the paper or phone form first. The answer should tell you fill it, skip it, or go to the right counter.
sections.quickSay: Show the form and keep your passport, boarding pass, or booking nearby if staff need to compare details.
sections.breakdown: Tôi có cần means do I need; điền vào means fill in; mẫu đơn này means this form; không makes it a yes/no question.

concreteTravelerValueImproved: turns a bare airport form question into a concrete counter-and-document moment

before.title: Khu vực hút thuốc ở đâu?
before.summary: Where is the smoking area?

after.title: Khu vực hút thuốc ở đâu?
after.summary: For finding the designated smoking area in an airport, station, mall, hotel, or attraction without guessing near the doors.

sections.atGlance: Ask staff before stepping outside or following a crowd. The answer is usually a gate, floor, balcony, or marked corner.
sections.quickSay: Point toward the terminal, lobby, or concourse if there are several exits. Wait for a gesture before walking.
sections.breakdown: Khu vực hút thuốc means smoking area; ở đâu asks where.

concreteTravelerValueImproved: grounds the smoking-area page in restricted terminal and venue navigation

before.title: Bạn có thể gọi đến nơi này và hỏi đường được không?
before.englishTitle: Can you call this place and ask for directions?
before.summary: Can you call this place and ask for directions?

after.title: Bạn có thể gọi đến nơi này và hỏi đường được không?
after.englishTitle: Can you call this place and ask for directions?
after.summary: For asking a hotel desk, driver, shop counter, or helper to call the destination when the map location is not enough.

sections.atGlance: Show the map location and phone number first. The helper needs the destination, not a long story.
sections.quickSay: Show the map location, address, station name, or sign first, ask once, and leave room for the answer.
sections.breakdown: Bạn có thể asks can you; gọi đến nơi này means call this place; và hỏi đường means and ask for directions; được không softens the request.

concreteTravelerValueImproved: makes the directions-call page a concrete map-location recovery moment

before.title: Chúng ta có thể ngồi bên trong được không?
before.summary: Can we sit inside?

after.title: Chúng ta có thể ngồi bên trong được không?
after.summary: For asking cafe or restaurant staff whether your group can take an indoor table instead of sitting outside.

sections.atGlance: Ask while pointing toward the indoor tables or doorway. The answer may depend on space, air conditioning, or reservations.
sections.quickSay: Keep the group visible and wait for a table, a no, or a point toward another seating area.
sections.breakdown: Chúng ta có thể means can we; ngồi bên trong means sit inside; được không softens the question.

concreteTravelerValueImproved: keeps bundled audio intact while grounding the page in indoor restaurant seating

before.title: Tôi có thể mượn máy sấy tóc được không?
before.englishTitle: Can I have a hair dryer?
before.summary: Can I have a hair dryer?

after.title: Tôi có thể mượn máy sấy tóc được không?
after.englishTitle: Can I have a hair dryer?
after.summary: For asking the hotel or homestay front desk to lend you a hair dryer for the room.

sections.atGlance: Ask with your room number or key card ready. Staff may send one up or hand it over at the desk.
sections.quickSay: Name the item, then show the room number if they need it. Keep the request small and practical.
sections.breakdown: Tôi có thể mượn means can I borrow; máy sấy tóc means hair dryer; được không softens the request.

concreteTravelerValueImproved: replaces literal can-have wording with a natural hotel borrowing request

before.title: Bạn có thể in biên lai được không?
before.summary: Can you print the receipt?

after.title: Bạn có thể in biên lai được không?
after.summary: For asking a cashier, hotel desk, clinic, pharmacy, or ticket counter to print a receipt before you leave.

sections.atGlance: Ask while the payment screen, bill, or purchase is still visible. It is easier before the next customer starts.
sections.quickSay: Keep the card, cash, room number, or booking nearby in case staff need to find the transaction.
sections.breakdown: Bạn có thể asks can you; in biên lai means print the receipt; được không softens the request.

concreteTravelerValueImproved: turns the receipt page into a concrete counter paperwork moment

before.title: Tôi có thể vào được không?
before.summary: Can I come in?

after.title: Tôi có thể vào được không?
after.summary: For asking permission before entering a room, office, clinic space, staff area, home, temple room, or small shop interior.

sections.atGlance: Pause at the doorway and ask before stepping in. A nod, hand wave, or shoe-removal gesture may be the answer.
sections.quickSay: Keep your body outside the threshold until they answer. The phrase works best with a small pause.
sections.breakdown: Tôi có thể means can I; vào means come in or enter; được không softens the question.

concreteTravelerValueImproved: makes the permission page a doorway etiquette moment instead of a generic yes-no page

before.title: Tôi có thể xem cái đó được không?
before.summary: Can I see that one?

after.title: Tôi có thể xem cái đó được không?
after.summary: For asking shop staff to show the item behind the counter, high on a shelf, inside a case, or across the stall.

sections.atGlance: Point to the exact item first. The phrase is clearer when staff can see which color, size, or display piece you mean.
sections.quickSay: Keep pointing until they reach for the right one. If there are several similar items, add a color or size card next.
sections.breakdown: Tôi có thể means can I; xem cái đó means see that one; được không softens the question.

concreteTravelerValueImproved: grounds the see-that-one page in a pointing-and-display shopping moment

before.title: Bạn có thể giảm giá cho tôi được không?
before.englishTitle: Can you give me a discount?
before.summary: Can you give me a discount?

after.title: Bạn có thể giảm giá cho tôi được không?
after.englishTitle: Can you give me a discount?
after.summary: For asking a market seller or flexible-price shop for a lower price after you already know the amount.

sections.atGlance: Ask while holding or pointing at one item. A smile and a pause keep the price talk light.
sections.quickSay: Let the seller answer with a new number, a calculator, or a firm no. Do not add a long explanation.
sections.breakdown: Bạn có thể asks can you; giảm giá cho tôi means give me a discount; được không softens the request.

concreteTravelerValueImproved: turns the discount page into a market-price moment with clear bargaining boundaries

before.title: Có được phép chụp ảnh không?
before.summary: Is photography allowed?

after.title: Có được phép chụp ảnh không?
after.summary: For checking photo rules before taking pictures in a museum, temple, exhibit, performance space, market stall, or tour site.

sections.atGlance: Ask before raising the camera or phone. Staff may point to a sign, a no-flash rule, or a restricted room.
sections.quickSay: Show the phone or camera if needed, then wait for yes, no, or a gesture toward the allowed area.
sections.breakdown: Có được phép means is it allowed; chụp ảnh means take photos; không makes it a yes/no question.

concreteTravelerValueImproved: turns the photography page into a concrete photo-rule check at attractions

before.title: Biển số xe không giống
before.summary: The car number is different

after.title: Biển số xe không giống
after.summary: For telling a driver, guard, or ride-hailing helper that the license plate does not match the car on your app.

sections.atGlance: Keep the ride screen open and compare the plate before getting in. This is a safety check, not a small wording detail.
sections.quickSay: Point to the app plate and then the vehicle plate. Wait for an explanation before opening the door.
sections.breakdown: Biển số xe means license plate; không giống means does not match.

concreteTravelerValueImproved: fixes car-number wording to a ride-hailing license-plate safety check

before.title: Xe buýt nào đi vào trung tâm thành phố?
before.englishTitle: Which bus goes to the city center?
before.summary: Which bus goes to the city center?

after.title: Xe buýt nào đi vào trung tâm thành phố?
after.englishTitle: Which bus goes to the city center?
after.summary: For asking station staff, airport staff, a kiosk, or another passenger which bus goes toward the city center before you board.

sections.atGlance: Ask before stepping onto the bus. Keep the destination or map visible so the answer can point to a route number or bay.
sections.quickSay: Point toward the buses or route board, then wait for a number, platform, or direction.
sections.breakdown: Xe buýt nào means which bus; đi vào means goes into; trung tâm thành phố means the city center.

concreteTravelerValueImproved: turns the bus page into a specific route-number and boarding decision moment

before.body: Move to table-for-two, wait-for-table, sit-by-fan, menu, or pay-the-bill cards if the seating exchange continues.
before.nearbyBody: Fan, table, menu, wait-time, and bill cards cover the seating and restaurant flow around this request.

after.body: After you get seated, move to ordering at the counter, waiting a long time, asking what they recommend, saying that's all, or paying.

phraseCards.english: Do we order here or at the counter?
I have been waiting a long time

after.nearbyBody: Ordering, wait-time, recommendations, closing the order, and payment cards cover the restaurant flow after seating.

concreteTravelerValueImproved: mirrors the richer rendered restaurant-flow card set in source and aligns visible body copy with the actual cards

before.title: Tôi có thể rửa tay ở đâu?
before.englishTitle: Where can I wash my hands?
before.summary: Where can I wash my hands?

after.title: Tôi có thể rửa tay ở đâu?
after.englishTitle: Where can I wash my hands?
after.summary: For finding a sink or hand-washing spot before eating, after a market stall, or after using a restroom.

sections.atGlance: Ask staff while pointing to your hands or soap. The answer is usually a restroom, sink, back room, or outside tap.
sections.quickSay: Keep it simple and follow the gesture. If they point to the restroom, ask for soap or paper only if you still need it.
sections.breakdown: Tôi có thể asks can I; rửa tay means wash my hands; ở đâu asks where.

concreteTravelerValueImproved: turns a bare hygiene question into a concrete sink/restroom handoff

before.title: Tôi sẽ nghĩ về nó
before.summary: I’ll think about it

after.title: Tôi sẽ nghĩ về nó
after.summary: For politely pausing a price, tour, service, or shopping decision without saying yes yet.

sections.atGlance: Use it after you hear the price or offer. It gives you room to step back without starting an argument.
sections.quickSay: Say it once, smile, and put the item, menu, or quote down if you are not ready to decide.
sections.breakdown: Tôi sẽ means I will; nghĩ về means think about; nó means it.

concreteTravelerValueImproved: makes the bargaining pause clear without turning it into a false yes

before.title: Hôm nay trời có mưa không?
before.summary: Will it rain today?

after.title: Hôm nay trời có mưa không?
after.summary: For checking the weather before you choose transport, clothes, a waiting spot, or an outdoor plan.

sections.atGlance: Ask when the sky is changing or staff seem to know the local pattern. A short yes, no, or maybe is enough.
sections.quickSay: Point outside or show the weather app if needed. Keep the question light; this is often small talk too.
sections.breakdown: Hôm nay means today; trời means the weather or sky; có mưa means rain; không makes it a yes/no question.

concreteTravelerValueImproved: turns the rain question into a practical planning and small-talk moment

before.title: Hãy lái xe cẩn thận
before.summary: Please drive carefully

after.title: Hãy lái xe cẩn thận
after.summary: For asking a taxi, ride-hailing, motorbike, or tour driver to drive more carefully when the ride feels unsafe.

sections.atGlance: Say it calmly and early. Pointing to the road, speed, seat belt, or traffic can make the request clearer.
sections.quickSay: Keep the line short. The driver needs the safety request more than a long explanation.
sections.breakdown: Hãy is a request marker; lái xe means drive; cẩn thận means carefully.

concreteTravelerValueImproved: grounds the safety request in a live vehicle moment without anxiety padding

before.title: Xin hãy lái xe chậm lại
before.summary: Please drive slower

after.title: Xin hãy lái xe chậm lại
after.summary: For asking a driver to slow down when speed, traffic, turns, or rain make the ride uncomfortable.

sections.atGlance: Say it before the next turn or fast stretch. A small hand-down gesture can help if words are not enough.
sections.quickSay: Say the line once, then pause. If nothing changes, follow with stop at the next corner or drive carefully.
sections.breakdown: Xin hãy means please; lái xe means drive; chậm lại means slow down.

concreteTravelerValueImproved: makes the slow-down page a direct ride-comfort tool

before.title: Hãy đánh dấu nó ở đây
before.summary: Please mark it here

after.title: Hãy đánh dấu nó ở đây
after.summary: For asking someone to mark the exact box, line, map spot, receipt item, or phone-screen place you need.

sections.atGlance: Point to the paper, map, or screen first. The phrase works best when the place to mark is already visible.
sections.quickSay: Hold the form or phone steady and pause. Let the other person circle, tick, underline, or tap the right spot.
sections.breakdown: Hãy is a request marker; đánh dấu means mark; nó means it; ở đây means here.

concreteTravelerValueImproved: turns the marking page into a precise form/map/screen handoff

before.title: Đó không phải là ý tôi
before.englishTitle: That is not what I meant
before.summary: That is not what I meant

after.title: Đó không phải là ý tôi
after.englishTitle: That is not what I meant
after.summary: For correcting a misunderstanding when the wrong item, place, number, route, or request is being used.

sections.atGlance: Use it before the mistake turns into payment, booking, food, or a ride. Keep the correction calm and specific.
sections.quickSay: Say the line, then point to the right item, screen, number, or address so the fix has somewhere to go.
sections.breakdown: Đó means that; không phải là means is not; ý tôi means what I meant or my meaning.

concreteTravelerValueImproved: makes the correction page practical without sounding confrontational

before.title: Tôi có thể thanh toán cho tài xế bằng thẻ không?
before.englishTitle: Can I pay the driver by card?
before.summary: Can I pay the driver by card?

after.title: Tôi có thể thanh toán cho tài xế bằng thẻ không?
after.englishTitle: Can I pay the driver by card?
